correctness.rationale: For each nonempty active support \(S\), the corresponding ideals form a true-twin clique of size \(w_S\), with \(w_{[r]}=\prod_i\ell_i-1\). Different supports have different closed neighborhoods because every singleton-support cell has at least two vertices. The quotient on nonempty supports has automorphism group \(S_r\), so only coordinate permutations preserving \(\ell_i\) lift between cells. The determining lower bound is forced by within-cell transpositions and is attained by fixing all but one vertex per cell. The distinguishing lower bound is forced by the unique largest full-support twin class, and an explicit injective color-subset construction with \(\prod_i\ell_i-1\) colors has trivial stabilizer.

value.rationale: The finding gives the complete graph automorphism group and two complementary symmetry-breaking invariants on an infinite natural algebraic family. The fully nonreduced hypothesis identifies a genuine structural regime in which every support is a nontrivial twin block; within that regime \(D+1=\prod_i\ell_i\) recovers a multiplicative invariant of the local chain lengths. This is not a recomputation of domination or zero forcing and provides reusable symmetry data for comparisons among ideal-intersection graphs.
